newsitem.title: HAITI: Poor Haitians riot and threaten Christmas shoppers.
newsitem.headline: Poor Haitians riot and threaten Christmas shoppers.

text.p: About 100 employees of the mayor's office in Delmas, a suburb of the capital, rioted in the streets on Tuesday, saying they had not been paid in months and could not afford Christmas celebrations.

The employeees were joined by other frustrated poor people, who turned against Christmas shoppers in the area. The mob took over about five square blocks, setting big fires in the streets, throwing rocks and menacing shoppers.
Witnesses reported that a group of young men with guns had threatened security guards outside a bank.
"It is Christmas but not for us because we don't have any money," one protester shouted. "We are tired of the rich people taking everything for themselves."

The riot caused local panic. Drivers of tap-taps, pickup trucks that provide the main public transportation, forced passengers out rather than drive through the chaos. Shoppers pushed into nearby stores to take cover.
There were no reports of injuries by midafternoon, after police and United Nations peacekeeping troops ended the disturbance and put out the fires.

Growing numbers of public employees have been demonstrating since the bankrupt government has not paid salaries for months or years. But hundreds of thousands of dollars are expected in Haiti through loans and gifts from international donors now that the government has approved a plan to privatise important businesses.
